title: Marketplace billing, entitlement & telemetry preflight notes
content:
Context and intent:
This is a working preflight for marketplace listings where billing units, entitlement flows, and telemetry need to align across Product, Engineering, Legal and GTM. The doc is intentionally granular (event names, SKU matrix, edge cases) so engineering and ops can do a final checklist before publishing.

High-level goals (why this doc exists):
- Prevent billing and entitlement mismatches at launch that cause unexpected chargebacks or trial leakage.
- Ensure telemetry provides guardrails for conversion experiments and incident triage.
- Provide copy snippets and UX suggestions to make entitlement/limits clear to customers and ISVs.

Quick status:
- Billing SKU matrix: draft v0.3 (needs finance signoff)
- Entitlement token mapping: prototype validated in sandbox (works for single-tenant; multi-tenant tests pending)
- Telemetry events: initial set implemented in staging, missing orthogonal fields for reseller flows
- Legal: draft contract clause bullets added, legal review scheduled 2025-01-17

1) Billing and SKU mapping checklist (engineering + finance):
- [ ] Authoritative SKU list exported to billing system (format: sku_id, sku_label, unit_type, unit_size, price_usd_monthly).
- [ ] Map Redwood internal model names -> marketplace SKU (avoid ambiguous names; e.g., do NOT use `redwood-large` in public SKU, use `dedicated-4x-A100` style).
- [ ] Metering semantics: tokens vs requests vs embeddings. Primary marketplace SKU should use tokens for Hosted API, embeddings per-embedding-unit for embeddings SKU.
- [ ] Trial entitlements: free trial credit maps to SKU_TRIAL_CREDIT (non-billable) and must not create invoiceable usage. Confirm upstream marketplace flags for credit-only grants.
- [ ] Overages policy: define whether overages auto-bill or block. Default recommendation: block with clear upgrade CTA.
- [ ] Billing test plan: purchases via vendor sandbox -> verify billing webhook -> reconcile sample invoice for 3 customers.
- Open questions:
  - Marketplace supports monthly and annual. Do we expose per-token discounts on annual? (Finance: threshold-based discount vs flat %).
  - Reseller flow: when reseller invoices, do we still emit end-customer usage telemetry at token-level or only aggregated? (ops preference: token-level pseudonymized telemetry for debugging).

2) Entitlement & access flow (product + infra):
- Goal: deterministic authorization checks to map marketplace entitlements to Redwood routes and capacity.
- Required artifacts:
  - Entitlement registry (CSV): entitlement_key, sku_id, allowed_routes, max_qps, kv_cache_size, burst_capacity
  - Redemption flow: marketplace -> Garmin (edge) -> Redwood auth service -> entitlement token (JWT) with claims {sku_id, expires_at, customer_id, tier}.
- Must-haves for launch:
  - TTL on entitlement tokens: 24 hours for frequent refresh; fallback to revalidate via API if token expired.
  - Rate-limiting hook names: rl.marketplace.sku_id, rl.marketplace.customer_id.
  - Canary: for first 72 hours route 20% of marketplace traffic to a special telemetry bucket so we can monitor errors and throttle misconfigurations.
- Edge cases and failure modes:
  - Partial provisioning: customer purchases SKU but entitlement not provisioned -> show clear UX error and open support ticket automatically.
  - Overlapping entitlements: customer has both reserved capacity + hosted API credits -> precedence rules: reserved capacity > credits > hosted rate limits. Document in entitlement registry.

3) Telemetry & observability (instrumentation + SRE):
- Required events (minimal):
  - marketplace.purchase (sku_id, customer_id, marketplace_tx_id, timestamp, billing_period)
  - entitlement.granted (sku_id, customer_id, token_id, expires_at, issued_by)
  - entitlement.redeemed (token_id, request_id, route, model, prompt_length, response_length, cost_estimate_tokens)
  - entitlement.denied (token_id, reason, request_id)
  - billing.adjustment (sku_id, customer_id, adjustment_type, amount_usd, reference_tx)
  - telemetry.debug.marketplace-sample (special marker for 1% of requests with full context)
- Event field standards: all events must include trace_id, environment (staging/prod), region, and redwood_customer_tier when available.
- Instrumentation checklist:
  - [ ] Add marketplace_tx_id to all relevant billing events and surface in invoices for reconciliation.
  - [ ] Ensure PII-free usage telemetry; hashed customer_id for vendor exports unless permitted.
  - [ ] Dashboard: marketplace purchases by SKU (24h, 7d, 30d), entitlement failures, top 10 deny reasons.
  - [ ] Alerts: entitlement.denied spikes > 5x baseline for 15m -> page devops oncall.

4) Listing copy & UX microcopy (GTM + design) – quick snippets to iterate in listing tile and detail page:
- Hero short: "Redwood Inference — low-latency LLM inference with pay-as-you-go tokens and dedicated reserved capacity."
- One-line value prop: "Predictable cost, enterprise SLA, and private deployment options for production LLMs."
- Feature bullets (tile):
  - "Hosted API: immediate access, token-based pricing, streaming responses."
  - "Dedicated capacity: reserved GPUs, predictable throughput, and SLA."
  - "Private deployments: VPC and on-prem packages with KMS/HSM integration."
- Entitlement microcopy examples (in console and listing):
  - Purchase confirmation: "This purchase grants {sku_label} for {billing_period}. You will receive an entitlement token to use in API calls."
  - Trial: "You have {trial_credits} free token credits valid for 30 days. No card required."
  - Failure: "Your marketplace entitlement could not be validated. Please retry or contact support (support@redwood.com)"
- UX tradeoffs to discuss:
  - Should trials appear as separate SKU tile or as a CTA on the main tile? (Pros: clarity vs fragmentation of listing metrics)

5) Legal & contract bullets (for listing and internal handoff):
- Add a short bullet on data residency: "No customer prompt data is stored outside the region unless explicitly opted-in." (requires legal approval)
- Refund policy: map to marketplace refund window; default: 14 days pro-rata for annual, 7 days for monthly unless gross misuse.
- Compliance callouts: note whether Private deployment customers require separate enterprise terms.

6) Launch runbook (ops checklist):
- Pre-launch (D-7): finance signoff on SKUs, legal signoff on copy, tech smoke tests green.
- D-1: marketplace listing in draft, assets uploaded (logos, screenshots, legal text), billing webhooks tested end-to-end.
- D0: open the listing but keep traffic gated behind rollout flag; randomly route 5% to marketplace flow.
- D+1: review telemetry, customer feedback, reconciliation of first invoices.
- D+3: increase traffic to 25% if no major issues.

7) Testing matrix (minimal tests we need automated or manual):
- Purchase flow via vendor sandbox (happy path).
- Entitlement TTL expiry and refresh behavior.
- Overlap scenarios: reserved capacity + hosted credit.
- Reseller scenario: reseller-signed purchase and end-customer usage visibility.
- Failed webhook reconciliation (simulate missing billing webhook).

8) Sample tickets / engineering owners:
- GTM-4321: SKU export -> billing system (owner: Marcus Liu)
- SRE-299: telemetry event schema validation and dashboard (owner: Diego Alvarez)
- PROD-501: entitlement expiry race condition (owner: Sophia Rivera)

Open notes / TODOs (quick brain dump):
- Validate reseller privacy with legal: can we expose token-level debug telemetry for reseller sales?
- Decide canonical names for SKUs vs model names. Propose prefix `mp-` for marketplace SKUs to avoid collisions.
- Add a small README for partner integrations team describing where to find the entitlement registry and how to add a new SKU (format + example).
- Consider adding a microcopy variant for EU customers about data residency and GDPR compliance.

Appendix: Example entitlement JWT payload (for engineering reference)
{"header":"{\"alg\":\"RS256\"}","claims":"{\n  \"iss\": \"marketplace.redwoodinference.com\",\n  \"sub\": \"cust_12345\",\n  \"sku\": \"mp-dedicated-4xA100\",\n  \"exp\": 1712345678,\n  \"tier\": \"enterprise\"\n}"}

Notes about the appendix: this is pseudocode to illustrate the required claims. The real schema will live in the entitlement registry CSV.

Contact/owners: Anika (owner of this doc + go-to-market), Marcus (finance/billing), Diego (SRE/telemetry), Sophie (product/legal liaison).

If you pick up a line item, add a short note below with date and initials. This doc will evolve into the formal launch checklist once finance/legal sign off.
